analysis.analysis: Three unrelated referents sharing the token 'tiger leap' are pulled into the composition as though they were sources for the archive's use of it: Estonia's Tiigrihupe education-digitisation programme, the e-Estonia successor programme, and an iOS network-diagnostic app. The Estonian programme is then given as an explanatory frame -- the composition glosses Tiger Leap as 'the boundary where machine-learning data collection expands out of tightly bound traditional schools', which is the Estonian schools framing bleeding into a viability-theory object. The name is inverted to 'Benjamin Walter'. And the dataset's own README states that the paper reaches the Tigersprung figure from control theory and DOES NOT CITE Benjamin; the composition supplies the citation the paper explicitly declines, then attaches two homonyms the paper never mentions. This is a distinct mechanism from the substitution observed at the bare-name address on the same day: there the entity is replaced, here the entity is correct and its frame is contaminated.
analysis.d: HOMONYM ACCRETION: THE ENTITY RESOLVES, THE FRAME DOES NOT. The leesharks datasets are named and described accurately, and three unrelated 'tiger leap' referents -- Estonia's Tiigrihupe, e-Estonia, and an iOS diagnostics app -- are attached as lineage. Walter Benjamin's name is inverted, and his Tigersprung, which the dataset's README names as the source of its title, is read into the figure correctly. (Corrected 2026-09-28: an earlier version of this record said the README declines the citation. The README says the paper reaches the figure from control theory without citing Benjamin, and that the dataset's name comes from his Tigersprung.)

findings: THE ENTITY RESOLVES CORRECTLY. Author named as contemporary author, poet and scholar; four leesharks datasets named individually and characterised accurately; the archive named as the object being built.
THREE HOMONYMS ATTACHED AS LINEAGE: Estonia's Tiigrihupe, the e-Estonia successor programme, and an Apple App Store network-diagnostic app, the last carried as source card 1.

THE ESTONIAN FRAME GOVERNS THE GLOSS: Tiger Leap is explained as a boundary where data collection 'expands out of tightly bound traditional schools' -- the education programme's framing imported into a viability-theory object.
NAME INVERSION: 'Benjamin Walter's philosophy of history'.

BENJAMIN READ RIGHTLY (corrected 2026-09-28). The tiger-leap README names the dataset after Benjamin's Tigersprung; the paper reaches the figure from control theory without citing him. The composition's Benjamin reading is correct, and the author reads the work as a development of Benjamin's tiger's leap; only the name inversion is a defect. An earlier version of this finding read the README as declining the citation.
DISTINCT MECHANISM FROM THE SAME-DAY BARE-NAME SUBSTITUTION: entity correct and frame contaminated, rather than entity replaced.
